messages:
Ciara: Quick note — residency metrics look inconsistent between eu-west and us-central for the same model shard. dashboard: <https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/kv-residency|kv-residency> shows eu reports ~78% while us reports ~12% for identical traffic profiles. anyone seen this?
Mike: Huh. Are we comparing same aggregation window and same sampler?
Ciara: using the 1m rollup we have in grafana (panel uses prom query `avg_over_time(kv_residency_ratio[1m])`). I pulled raw samples too: eu shard A: [0.81,0.79,0.77], us shard A: [0.13,0.12,0.11]. logs show similar request mix.
Oliver: Could be normalization to alloc size — are we dividing by node_memory_total or by expected_kv_capacity?
Tess: Also eviction counters differ. us had a big bump in `kv_evictions_total` around the same time window. Might be aggressive eviction policy fallthrough.
Ciara: pasted quick prom queries: ```promql
sum by (region) (rate(kv_residency_bytes_total[5m])) / sum by (region) (kv_allocated_bytes)
```
results: eu ~0.78, us ~0.11.
Mike: That division looks right. Do you have the raw allocation tags? maybe us nodes are on smaller GPUs?
Ciara: same instance type per infra inventory; verified config: `kv.alloc_bytes=24GB` across both clusters.
metrics-bot: Alert: kv_residency_ratio(us-central) dropped below 0.2 for 3m (alert id #KVR-421).
Tess: Could be sampling bias — our sampler currently picks every Nth key based on consistent hash; with long-running sessions keys cluster and sampler misses hot shards. We saw this before with long contexts.
Oliver: Proposed fix: change rollup to use reservoir sampling per shard and include `session_count` denom: `kv_residency_ratio_normalized = sum(residency_bytes)/sum(max(kv_allocated_bytes, session_count * avg_kv_per_session))`. Might need a new gauge `kv_active_sessions`.
Mike: I can add a diagnostic panel that shows residency vs active_sessions and eviction_rate side-by-side. Would help prove the normalizer.
Ciara: Also want to capture eviction labels: `kv_evictions_total{reason="lru"}` vs `reason="compaction"` — right now eviction counter is undifferentiated.
Tess: +1. If compaction spikes we should not treat it same as LRU-driven eviction for health checks.
infra-bot: Deploy started: perf-probe/kv-residency-diagnostics @ciara (deploy id 2024-11-02-08:22)
Ciara: FYI saw a 95th pct latency bump yesterday that aligns with residency drop — linking perf trace: <https://traces.internal/trace/0xabc|trace-0xabc>. Suspect memory churn => kernel selection falling back to slow path.
Oliver: Good catch. Kernel fallback path logs show more memcpy/backing-page faults when residency < 0.25. We should drive alert thresholds off normalized residency, not raw bytes.
Mike: Action items: 1) add kv_active_sessions gauge (ikennes to implement?) 2) break out eviction reasons in exporter (Tess) 3) new dashboard tile: residency_normalized, eviction_by_reason, active_sessions trend (me) 4) temporary: raise residency alert threshold for us region until sampler change deployed (Ciara)
Ciara: I'll file a short playbook for oncall: how to triage residency dips (check active_sessions, eviction_reason, kernel-fallback logs, correlate with latency traces). Will post link when done. :memo:
Tess: One more ask — can we tag residency samples with `sampling_window` label so rollups are comparable across dashboards? small change in exporter.
Mike: Agree. makes diffs sane.
Ciara: Thanks all. If someone can start the exporter PR I'll review. I'll also attach the short CSV snapshots I pulled to the playbook.
Oliver: I'll grep kernel-fallback logs and add a small alert if memcpy_count > 100/s.
metrics-bot: Note: Next metrics rollup at 2024-11-03T00:00Z.
Ciara: closing loop — created issue infra #987: "Normalize kv residency signal and add eviction reason labels". Assigned to Mike/Tess.
